request.operation: independent review of the ThinkingCap secondary output-cap correction

findings_summary.classification: confirmed and resolved by the proposed correction
findings_summary.finding: A 4096-token router output cap contradicts the retained passing quality protocol and would truncate three successful CS attempts.
findings_summary.evidence: The quality artifact declares 8192 reasoning-headroom tokens plus 2048 visible-answer tokens, sends max_completion_tokens=10240 for every attempt, and records three normal-stop CS completions of 5217 tokens, including 5058 reasoning tokens.
findings_summary.resolution: Advertise max_output_tokens=10240 while preserving the 131072 total-context contract.

artifacts.claim_limit: The 10240 value is the qualified maximum completion budget. The retained near-limit context suite used a 4096-token completion allowance, so it does not prove a 10240-token completion at the largest tested prompt. Total prompt plus completion remains bounded by 131072.

advisory_priors: The 8192 reasoning and 2048 visible values are one combined completion cap; the endpoint does not hard-partition the two channels.
C1 and the up-to-two-image capability are unchanged by this metadata correction.

recommendation.reason: 10240 exactly matches the retained qualification budget and avoids truncating known passing responses; 4096 is not evidence-consistent.

human_gate_note: The existing user authorization covers this necessary correction to the already-approved secondary promotion.
